handoff.purpose: Analyze a capture of DOM/CSSOM geometry and computed style to produce objective (Tier A) and proxy (Tier B) metrics for design quality, plus a comparison table.

symbols.name: BANNED_FACES
symbols.note: Tuple of font family names considered generated defaults.

symbols.name: _looks_like_identifier
symbols.note: Heuristic to detect internal identifiers or raw JSON in user-facing text.

symbols.name: _lum
symbols.note: Computes relative luminance of an RGB tuple.

symbols.name: contrast_ratio
symbols.note: Computes WCAG contrast ratio between two RGB colors.

symbols.name: Metric
symbols.note: Dataclass representing one measurement with evidence.

symbols.name: Metric.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes the metric, truncating offenders to 12.

symbols.name: _sel
symbols.note: Builds a short selector string for an element.

symbols.name: _is_panel
symbols.note: Determines if an element is a framed panel.

symbols.name: _contains
symbols.note: Checks geometric containment with strictly smaller area.

symbols.name: analyse
symbols.note: Main analysis function producing a report dict with metrics.

symbols.name: compare
symbols.note: Builds a side-by-side text table of metrics across reports.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: Reads capture JSON files, analyses them, writes report.json, prints table.

claims.text: No pixels are inspected; every number here is derived from geometry and computed style
claims.why: console_errors (line ~143) is not geometry or computed style; identifier_leaks (line ~171) is text-based. The claim is too broad.

claims.text: Tier A metrics ... can gate.
claims.why: No gating logic is present in this chunk; only metric generation.

claims.text: Tier B metrics are PROXIES for a judgement no rule can make.
claims.why: All Tier B metrics are heuristics (e.g., framed_panels, allcaps_text_share, status_pills_visible) rather than objective pass/fail checks.

claims.text: Each proxy carries its own agreement record, and a proxy that stops tracking the human verdict gets retired rather than defended.
claims.why: No agreement record or retirement mechanism appears in this chunk; likely in other modules.

claims.text: Every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it, so a disagreement is inspectable instead of arguable.
claims.why: visible_elements (line ~146) and allcaps_text_share (line ~162) do not include an offenders list, so they do not return the elements behind them.

claims.text: Thresholds are stamped ASSUMED until the corpus is large enough to earn MEASURED.
claims.why: No threshold stamping is present in this chunk; likely in other modules.

claims.text: Right now the corpus is n=4 (three rejected surfaces, one approved), which is enough to set direction and nowhere near enough to gate on.
claims.why: No corpus data is present in this chunk; only the claim itself.

claims.text: stdlib only, by design
claims.why: Imports are json, math, collections, dataclasses, pathlib — all stdlib.

claims.text: Faces that read as a generated default. Not a quality judgement about the typeface — a statement about what every AI dashboard already wears.
claims.why: The constant lists common default faces and the comment explicitly avoids a quality judgement.

claims.text: Text that is a leaked internal name rather than something a person would say.
claims.why: The function returns true for JSON-like strings and snake_case identifiers, which matches the description.

claims.text: A framed surface, not a hairline divider or a text run.
claims.why: Requires borderSides >= 1 and minimum dimensions, excluding hairlines and small text runs.

claims.text: WCAG AA: 4.5:1 body, 3.0:1 large
claims.why: The code sets need=3.0 for large text and 4.5 otherwise, matching WCAG AA.

claims.text: interactive targets should reach 44x44
claims.why: The code flags interactive elements with width or height < 44.

claims.text: grotesk defaults that mark a generated page
claims.why: The code counts distinct banned font families found in elements.

claims.text: a broken page is not a design question
claims.why: The metric simply counts console errors as an objective issue.

claims.text: raw density of what is on screen at once
claims.why: The metric uses cap['elementsKept'] as a count of visible elements.

claims.text: when everything is a bordered box, nothing is elevated
claims.why: The metric counts panels, and the note explains the design concern.

claims.text: more than two or three corner radii reads as unconsidered
claims.why: The metric counts distinct radius values; the note expresses the design heuristic.

claims.text: frames inside frames inside frames
claims.why: The metric calculates the deepest nested chain of panels.

claims.text: shouted micro-labels used as decoration rather than hierarchy
claims.why: The metric measures the share of all-caps text, which aligns with the note.

claims.text: if everything is flagged, nothing is flagged
claims.why: The metric counts status pills; the note explains the concern.

claims.text: an N-equal-tile metric row is the most recognisable trope in the category
claims.why: The metric detects rows of equal-sized tiles.

claims.text: distinct 30-degree hue families in use, semantic colour included
claims.why: The metric buckets hues into 30-degree families and counts those with at least two occurrences.

claims.text: internal field names and raw JSON rendered as user-facing text
claims.why: The metric uses _looks_like_identifier to detect such strings.

claims.text: Side-by-side table. The point of the whole exercise: do the numbers separate the surfaces a human rejected from the one he approved?
claims.why: The function produces a side-by-side table of metric values, allowing visual separation.

claims.text: usage: python -m daedalus.gui.lint runs/gui/*.json
claims.why: The code prints exactly this usage when no arguments are given.

claims.text: full evidence written to runs/gui/report.json
claims.why: The code writes to Path('runs/gui/report.json') and prints that message.

observations.what: The module docstring claims 'every number here is derived from geometry and computed style' but console_errors and identifier_leaks are text-based, not geometry.
The module docstring claims 'every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it' but visible_elements and allcaps_text_share do not include offenders.
The module docstring claims 'thresholds are stamped ASSUMED until the corpus is large enough to earn MEASURED' but no threshold stamping is present in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'a proxy that stops tracking the human verdict gets retired rather than defended' but no retirement mechanism is present in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'the corpus is n=4' but no corpus data is present in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'reads a capture from probe.js' but analyse takes a dict and main reads JSON files; the actual capture reading is in main.
The module docstring claims 'Tier A metrics ... can gate' but no gating logic is present in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'each proxy carries its own agreement record' but no agreement record is present in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'metrics over the DOM/CSSOM' but consoleErrors is not DOM/CSSOM.
The module docstring claims 'no pixels are inspected' but contrast_ratio uses colors which may come from pixels; however, this chunk only processes computed style values.
The module docstring claims 'you can always point at the elements that produced a count' but console_errors and allcaps_text_share do not point to elements.
The module docstring claims 'the rules must not [need a browser]' but the capture is from probe.js; however, the rules themselves are pure functions.
The module docstring claims 'a disagreement is inspectable instead of arguable' but no disagreement record format is shown in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'reproducible and explainable' but no randomness is used, so it is reproducible.

The module docstring claims 'the point of the whole exercise: do the numbers separate the surfaces a human rejected from the one he approved?' but compare only prints a table and does not compute separation.
